follow-up time: Minimum 1 year, up to 2 years for children with circulating HCV RNA
exposure: HCV viral load (<6 log copies/ml vs. >=6 log copies/ml)
cohort: 214 pregnant women with positive HCV serology from six hospitals in Southern France
finding: While HIV/HCV co-infection and higher HCV viral load were associated with higher rates of neonatal HCV transmission, no specific obstetric practices during labor and childbirth were found to be associated with an increased risk.
mod_finding: No specific obstetric practices during labor and childbirth, including type of induction, monitoring of labor, route of delivery, and perineal obstetric maneuvers, were associated with an increased rate of HCV maternal-fetal transmission.
followup_time: Minimum 1 year, up to 2 years for children with circulating HCV RNA
